latest_release.name: CodeAssist 3.47.0
latest_release.body:
# 🚀 CodeAssist 3.47.0

**C# ON YOUR PHONE (NEW PLUGIN)**
- A new **C# plugin** with .NET 10 and the Roslyn compiler on the device: install it from Get plugins (arm64 and x86_64 devices)
- **Compile and run** C# console programs, with `.csproj` support, **NuGet package restore** and project references
- Errors and warnings as you type, completion (including types not yet imported, which adds the `using`), parameter help and quick fixes for usings
- **Go to declaration, find usages, rename, quick documentation**, semantic coloring, the outline and code folding
- **Reformat** with Roslyn's own formatter
- **Run xUnit, NUnit and MSTest tests** from the gutter or the Run picker, with results in the Tests tab
- A module with several programs gets a Run row for each

**STABILITY**
- Fixed the most common crash of 3.46.0: a list given the same entry twice closed the app, most often right after opening a project. The app's lists are now guarded against it
- Fixed the top "app not responding" freeze: a file with one **very long line** (a minified script, a page with an inlined image) froze the editor. A line is now drawn up to 10,000 columns and marked as cut; the rest is still in the file and is searched, edited and saved as usual
- Lines past 20,000 columns are drawn without syntax colors, which keeps typing in them fast and uses far less memory
- A collapsed fold on a very long line no longer slows the editor

**FOLDABLES AND TABLETS**
- Dialogs, the first-launch tour and the split view **respect the hinge** of a half-opened foldable: nothing is drawn across the fold
- A docked side pane ends at the fold, so the Files panel has one side and the code the other
- The first-launch tour and the side panes fit an unfolded foldable
- The **keyboard symbol bar** shows on foldables and tablets, with a setting to turn it off
- On a narrow tablet the home title is no longer cut off

**EDITOR**
- The **line number bar can scroll sideways** with the code
- Kotlin: the editor reports ordinary compile errors it used to miss, and completes after more receivers
- Kotlin: a setter's parameter name completes to `value`
- A tool window can be opened in zen mode on a phone in landscape
- **Blocks** is offered only on files it works for; a tab saved in Blocks mode on another file reopens as code

**LOOK AND FEEL**
- Lighter secondary text, standard Material controls on the settings pages and the New Project form
- One back arrow on every screen, and written dates on the Daily tab in your language
- Tonal template cards in New Project; the plain JVM module type is named **Java Module**
- A fresh install no longer shows notices meant for people upgrading from an older version
- The analytics consent sheet keeps its buttons on screen
- The store item header stays readable on Android 11 and older

**DEPENDENCIES AND EXPORT**
- The repositories dialog **suggests common repositories** and explains a rejected address
- Jars an AAR bundles under `libs/` reach the build
- A library exported as a Gradle project is **ready to publish**, on JitPack included, and the Export screen says what the export contains

**PLUGINS**
- A plugin's run mark and its module's Run card no longer need the IDE's internals (plugin API 3.7.0)
- The plugin API artifacts can be built by JitPack

Full changelog: https://github.com/tyron12233/CodeAssist/releases/tag/v3.47.0

# CodeAssist [![CI](https://img.shields.io/github/actions/workflow/status/tyron12233/CodeAssist/ci.yml?branch=main&label=CI)](https://github.com/tyron12233/CodeAssist/actions) [![Release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/tyron12233/CodeAssist?display_name=tag&sort=semver)](https://github.com/tyron12233/CodeAssist/releases) [![License](https://img.shields.io/github/license/tyron12233/CodeAssist)](LICENSE) [![Discord](https://img.shields.io/badge/chat-Discord-5865F2)](https://discord.gg/y2gycT6pDW) CodeAssist is an IDE for Android that runs on Android. You can write Kotlin and Java, preview Compose and XML layouts, and build, sign and install APKs on the phone itself, without a computer or a remote build server. A desktop version for Windows and Linux is built from the same code.

## Features - Kotlin and Java editing: completion, auto-import, errors as you type with quick fixes, go to definition/implementation, reformat and optimize imports. - Android XML completion and validation for layouts, manifests and resource files. - Compose `@Preview` functions render next to the code and update as you edit. XML layouts preview too, including your own custom views. - Builds run on the device: aapt2, kotlinc, ecj, D8/R8 and apksigner. Builds are incremental. Output can be a debug APK, or a release APK or App Bundle signed with your own key. - Multi-module projects, build variants, ViewBinding, AIDL, KSP (Room, Hilt) and Firebase's `google-services.json`. - Dependencies from Maven Central, Google's Maven repository, and local JAR and AAR files. - Import an existing Gradle project, or export a project as a Gradle project to open in Android Studio. - Git: clone, commit, branch, merge, stash and push. With a GitHub sign-in you can clone private repositories and open pull requests. - An optional AI coding agent that uses your own API key (Anthropic, Gemini, OpenAI or OpenRouter). - Plugins can add languages, build steps, tool windows and project templates. C/C++ (NDK) support is a separate plugin. ## Limitations - CodeAssist does not run Gradle. Build scripts are read when a project is imported (dependencies, version catalogs, the common `android {}` options), but Gradle plugins and custom build logic are not executed. - Only the bundled Kotlin compiler plugins are available: Compose, kotlinx.serialization and Parcelize. - Kotlin support is newer than Java support and has more rough edges. - Large projects are slow to index and build on phones with little RAM. If something you need is missing, open an issue. It helps to know what people are trying to build. ## Download - [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/tyron12233/CodeAssist/releases): the Android APK, and the desktop builds for Windows and Linux. - [Google Play](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.tyron.code) The Play build and the GitHub APK are signed with different keys, so one can't be installed over the other. ## How it works Gradle is too heavy to run on a phone, so CodeAssist keeps its own project model. Each module's build is a graph of tasks with up-to-date checks, much like Gradle's, and the tasks call the Android tools directly instead of going through the Android Gradle Plugin. Changing one file only re-runs the tasks that depend on it. Java analysis uses Eclipse JDT. Kotlin uses the Kotlin compiler's parser with CodeAssist's own analysis on top, so completion doesn't have to start a full compiler session on every keystroke. Symbol indexes for libraries and the Android SDK are stored on disk and read in place, which keeps memory use flat as projects grow. Compose previews don't install anything. The project's compiled code runs in a bytecode interpreter inside the IDE, against the real Compose runtime. More detail is in [docs/architecture.md](docs/architecture.md), and the full list of documents is in [docs/README.md](docs/README.md). ## Building from source You need JDK 17 or newer (CI uses JDK 25). The Android SDK is only needed for the full build. ```sh # Core modules only: plain JVM, no Android SDK needed CI_CORE_ONLY=true ./gradlew check # Everything, including the Compose UI and the Android app ./gradlew build # Run the desktop IDE ./gradlew :ide-desktop:run # Build the Android app ./gradlew :ide-android:assembleDebug ``` ## Project layout ``` platform/ core services with no IDE-specific knowledge; everything depends on it lang/ the language SPI, indexes, analysis, and the Java/Kotlin/XML backends build-system/ the incremental task engine and the JVM build pipelines run/ running project code on device: interpreter, bytecode VM, AWT/Swing android/ Android support: facets, variants, SDK data, layout preview services/ dependencies, version control, the project store, analytics, the AI agent plugins/ the plugin SPI and the host that loads plugins app/ the Compose UI and the Android, desktop and command-line launchers tools/ test harnesses ``` Gradle project paths are flat (`:lang-kotlin` lives in `lang/lang-kotlin`); `settings.gradle.kts` maps them. [docs/modules.md](docs/modules.md) describes each module. ## Tests and benchmarks Completion quality, editor latency, indexing and build performance are checked against committed baselines by the `regressionTest` tasks. The numbers below are regenerated on each release. | Area | Metric | Result | |---|---|---| | Java completion **quality** | recall / top-1 / MRR | **100%** / 75% / 0.88 | | Java completion **latency** (per keystroke) | member access / type ref | **4.3 ms** / 2.8 ms | | Symbol **index** quality | recall / top-1 / MRR | **100%** / 90% / 0.95 | | Symbol **index** query | prefix / fuzzy | ~4.4 µs / ~56 ns | Recall is how often the expected item appears in the completion list at all, top-1 how often it is first, and MRR the average of 1/rank. Latency is measured on the maintainer's machine, so treat it as a rough figure. **2595** tests passing across **442** suites · 0 failing · 4 skipped (framework / `CI_CORE_ONLY`). ## Contributing Bug reports and pull requests are welcome. For anything larger than a small fix, open an issue first so we can agree on the approach. Before sending a pull request, run `CI_CORE_ONLY=true ./gradlew check`; it is what CI runs. Plugin authors should start with [docs/writing-plugins.md](docs/writing-plugins.md). For questions and discussion, join the [Discord server](https://discord.gg/y2gycT6pDW). ## License CodeAssist is licensed under the GNU General Public License v3.0 or later. See [LICENSE](LICENSE). The plugin SPI modules (`plugin-api`, `plugin-ui-api`, `platform-core`, `vfs-api`, `project-model-api`, `language-api`, `index-api`, `analysis-api` and `build-api`, published under `io.github.tyron12233`) also carry the Classpath exception (see [LICENSE-EXCEPTION](LICENSE-EXCEPTION)), so a plugin compiled against them can use any license. The license covers the code, not the name. A modified build needs its own name, icon and application id: see [TRADEMARKS.md](TRADEMARKS.md).
